reference.visible_appearance: Short thick tousled medium-brown hair, clean-shaven face, unobstructed nearly frontal face turned slightly toward image left, light gray long-sleeved crew-neck knit sweater. Seated with visible shoulders and torso. No glasses. Lower body and shoes not shown.
reference.visual_limits: Softly blurred green/tan background with a bright yellow chair; white tabletop and cup at lower right. Recommended for facial identity; do not import the chair/table into generated output.
reference.inspection: Original downloaded without image editing, decoded with macOS sips, and visually inspected through view_image.

alternate_not_recommended.reason: More side-on face, other people and microphone; less suitable than selected reference.

event.label: one brief right-hand V/face-framing gesture, followed by release into an outward arm spread
event.type: brief face gesture amid distinct arm and body action switches

surrounding_actions.action: bent-knee side stepping with both wrists drooped in front of torso; one brief earlier hand flick occurs within this phase
right arm extends to point outward; brief transition immediately before target
hand/arm release, then bilateral arms rise and cross overhead
bilateral overhead-to-side spread, alternating lateral lean/leg extension

prompts.A: Change only the main performer's black dress to bright red, preserving its shape, white collar and cuffs, and existing ribbon. Preserve the same person, face, hair, accessories, skin, body proportions, room, objects, background, camera, composition and all original motion. Preserve every original gesture, expression, action order, speed, timing and rhythm. Keep the same realistic live-action appearance.
prompts.B_addition: In particular, preserve the single brief right-hand V-shaped face-framing gesture around 2.08–2.75 seconds: the right hand approaches the eye/face, briefly forms the V beside or across the face, then moves away into the arm spread. Preserve the concurrently bent and lifted leg. Keep this local gesture between the preceding bent-knee stepping and arm pointing or sweep and the following overhead arm movement and broad sideways spread. Keep all these original actions at their original times; do not skip, merge, prolong, repeat or move the brief face gesture, and do not damage the surrounding rhythm.

limitations: A cat moves in the background; do not confuse cat motion with performer motion.
Source includes baked-in letterboxing and a watermark; no source cleanup was applied.

An earlier ~38.4-38.6 s hand-to-mouth/cheek flick is present; the coarse-scan statement that the preceding microgesture was absent was too strong. Its exact shape is blurrier and it is not the selected target. No matched-monocle claim is made.
All 141 normalized frames plus dense native target frames were inspected; the entire 177-frame native-window sequence was not separately exhaustively reviewed.
Both real recordings and the animation share a choreography family; no cross-choreography generality or exact matched-event claim.
Full gesture about0.67seconds; not a less-than0.5second complete event, and not assumed absent from2FPS semantic sampling.
